# Mastering Comments in VS Code for Laravel Developers: Beyond Ctrl + / As developers working with PHP frameworks like Laravel, code readability and efficient commenting are paramount. When you dive into large files, the way you comment code directly impacts how quickly you can understand legacy code or collaborate with a team. Many developers default to the simple `Ctrl + /` shortcut in VS Code, but this often leads to frustration when you need more nuanced control over your comments—especially when dealing with specific syntax requirements like HTML comments versus PHP block comments. This post dives deep into how you can achieve precise and syntactically correct commenting within VS Code for your Laravel projects, moving beyond the basic line-comment functionality. ## The Limitations of the Default Comment Shortcut The ubiquitous `Ctrl + /` shortcut in VS Code is incredibly useful for quickly toggling single-line comments. However, as you noted, it typically inserts PHP-style block comments (`//`) or C-style block comments (`{{-- ... --}}`). When working with Blade files, HTML views, or mixed PHP/HTML structures, this default behavior often clashes with the desired syntax, specifically when aiming for standard HTML comments like ``. For instance, if you select text and use the shortcut, VS Code defaults to inserting the appropriate PHP comment structure, which isn't what you want if your goal is pure HTML commenting. We need methods that allow us to define *what kind* of comment we are creating. ## Strategy 1: Leveraging Multi-line Comment Syntax The most robust solution lies in understanding and utilizing standard multi-line comment syntax explicitly. Instead of relying solely on line-based shortcuts, mastering the language-specific block comments gives you full control. ### Using Standard Block Comments for Clarity For commenting large blocks of code or HTML structures within your Laravel views (Blade files) or configuration files, stick to the native syntax: ```html

This entire section is commented out.

``` When you use these standard markers, VS Code’s built-in handling becomes much more predictable. While there isn't a single universal shortcut that perfectly swaps between `{{--` and `` for HTML blocks, `//` or `/* */` for PHP logic, and ensuring your IDE settings support these conventions. By understanding the context of your file type and leveraging VS Code’s extension ecosystem, you transform basic shortcuts into powerful tools that keep your code clean, readable, and maintainable. Stop fighting the default behavior; start customizing your environment to match your development philosophy.
